falsification.not_applicable: a registration: the branch changes docs/roadmaps/roadmap.yaml, three receipts under docs/audits/, its evidence under .quorum/evidence/ and this receipt, and no code, so there is no hunk to revert. Each row's notes: carries the falsifier its future implementation must pass (pin X, run with binary Y, assert refusal; change one source byte, assert Update with no host access; drift against an empty lock, assert a distinguishable exit), and the measurements behind the rows are quoted with their run ids and counts so they can be re-taken.

crux.verdict: accept refuse-by-default for PMAT-579: OpenTofu 1.8.5 RUN locally refuses on both init and plan with exit 1 and no flag; Terraform and Pulumi READ at source do the same as an error, and OpenTofu is named as Terraform's fork so the two count as one lineage. Reject Ansible's posture, which defaults a mismatch to a warning and passes a check it cannot evaluate. forjar today neither refuses nor warns, which is what the row registers. PMAT-581 and PMAT-582 were not surveyed and the survey says so; each owes its own at implementation.
